Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-04
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-31

To the Cigna National Appeals Unit:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed based on the clinical documentation summarized below.

**Policy criteria at issue**

My understanding is that Cigna applies the EviCore "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines," policy CMM-318, "Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Resurfacing/Revision/Arthrodesis," to precertification requests for CPT 23472. The version of this policy I was able to review (effective August 1, 2024) states:

"Total shoulder arthroplasty (replacement) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:
- Radiographic imaging and/or an advanced diagnostic procedure (i.e., MRI, CT) is conclusive for the presence of advanced destructive degenerative joint disease (i.e., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis) with marked narrowing of the joint space that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings including ANY of the following: Irregular joint surfaces; Glenoid sclerosis; Glenoid osteophyte changes; Flattened glenoid; Cystic changes in the humeral head.
- Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment) for at least three (3) months.
- Failure of at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management."

I note that Cigna's own published policy-update materials indicate that CMM-318 underwent a further revision effective March 7, 2026, which was current at the time my request was denied. I was not able to independently confirm whether the wording of the "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (Replacement) Indications" section changed between the August 2024 version quoted above and the version effective March 7, 2026. I am therefore not quoting the March 2026 version, and I ask Cigna to confirm, in its response to this appeal, the exact current criteria it applied to my request and to explain any differences from the language quoted above.

**How my records meet each criterion**

1. Radiographic/imaging findings of advanced destructive degenerative joint disease with marked joint-space narrowing and correlating findings:
Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) obtained 2026-05-21 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. These findings include at least two of the specific findings listed in the policy criterion — glenoid osteophyte changes and a flattened glenoid — and directly correlate with my reported symptoms and physical exam findings (glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees). CT imaging performed at the same time additionally confirmed an intact rotator cuff, ruling out rotator cuff tear arthropathy as a confounding diagnosis.

2. Function-limiting pain for at least three months:
My symptoms consist of progressive shoulder pain that has been present for 9 months, unrelieved by rest, which is well in excess of the three-month minimum in the policy. This pain is function-limiting: I am unable to reach overhead, unable to dress without assistance, and unable to sleep on the affected side. These functional limitations are consistent with the policy's example of "loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living."

3. Failure of at least three months of provider-directed non-surgical management:
I have completed the following provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which in total spans well over three months without adequate relief:
- NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-03-23, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- Supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, 16 visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-12 through 2026-06-21), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of pain or restoration of function.
Taken together, this course of conservative care — medication, injection, and supervised physical therapy — represents more than three months of provider-directed non-surgical management that has failed to relieve my symptoms or restore function.

**Additional relevant clinical facts**

I have no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, orthopedic surgery, has recommended total shoulder arthroplasty based on the imaging findings, examination, and failure of conservative management described above.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, I ask that Cigna reverse the denial of prior authorization for CPT 23472 (total shoulder arthroplasty) and approve the requested surgery as medically necessary. If Cigna's medical director continues to find that the submitted records do not satisfy the applicable criteria, I request a written, specific explanation identifying which criterion is not met and the exact current policy language (including section, version, and effective date) relied upon, so that my provider and I may respond directly.

I have enclosed the following supporting documentation with this appeal:
- Shoulder radiographs and report, 2026-05-21
- CT imaging and report, 2026-05-21
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-12 through 2026-06-21, 16 visits)
- Documentation of corticosteroid injection, 2026-03-23
- Medication history (NSAID trial, 4 months)
- Office notes/exam findings from Dr. Okafor
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor
- A copy of the original denial notice (Reference Number POC-B9867C3E93-20631)

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Okafor of the outcome in writing. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31, and I am submitting well within that deadline. If any additional information is needed to complete this review, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my surgeon's office at [surgeon office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Rowan Grant
